metadata.note: The Chicago, Burlington and Quincy's branch from Frannie, Wyoming southwest 42.4 miles through Mantua, Garland, Powell, Ralston and Corbett to Cody - the only passenger railroad Cody ever had, and the reason the town became the eastern rail gateway to Yellowstone. The first train reached Cody November 11 1901. The CB&Q marketed the connection hard, as 'The Cody Road into Yellowstone Park' from 1905, running motor coaches on from the railhead over the 96-mile government road to Lake Hotel and building the Burlington Cody Cafe (1917) and Cody Inn (1922) to hold park-bound passengers overnight. Passenger service ended in 1956. The line still exists as BNSF's Cody Subdivision, freight only, which is where the geometry comes from - and, per Rule 1, is why the drawn years stop at 1956 rather than following the rails to the present. The trains that fed this branch reached Frannie over the Pryor Mountains from Toluca, Montana until April 1911, and afterwards over the Clarks Fork route from Billings via Fromberg, Bridger and Warren; neither of those connecting lines is drawn here. The main line this branch met at Frannie is now on the map as cbq_big_horn_basin_line.geojson (Billings - Frannie - Greybull - Thermopolis - Casper - Orin Junction).
sources: https://pryormountains.org/-homestead-era/railroad (construction, opening November 11 1901, station order, the April 1911 abandonment of Toluca-Warren and the Fromberg-Warren relocation)
https://www.geyserbob.com/cody-wy (Burlington Cody Cafe June 20 1917, Cody Inn June 19 1922, YPTCo coach connections, end of passenger service in 1956, 1957 auction)

https://www.environmentandsociety.org/exhibitions/cbq-railroad/national-park-line (CB&Q as the Yellowstone 'National Park Line', 1905 'Cody Road' brochure, direct east-entrance service from 1912, the 96-mile Cody road)

https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/wyomingrrs.pdf (John Fowler, Wyoming Railroads - Passenger Stations & Stops, SL 170, line 11 Frannie-Cody: mileposts Frannie 0.0, Mantua 9.9, Garland 14.8, Powell 19.8, Ralston 25.8, Corbett 35.8, Cody 42.4, with 1909/1925/1932 public-timetable coverage and absence from the 1950 timetable)

not_yet_sourced: No timetable was consulted for this branch. Every headway_min is an estimate and avg_speed_kmh is a guess; the number of daily trains, whether service was daily or daily-except-Sunday, and the train numbers are all unknown here.

SOURCE CONFLICT on the end date: secondary sources say passenger service to Cody ended in 1956, but the branch's stations are already absent from the 1950 CB&Q public timetable. The most likely reconciliation is that the last years were an unadvertised mixed train, but nothing consulted states that. If a source shows the last advertised passenger train ran before 1950 and nothing carried passengers afterwards, the third segment's start and end should be revisited under Rule 1.

The 1901-1911 approach to Frannie from Toluca, Montana over Pryor Gap (87 miles, stations Ronald, Mifflin, Coburn, Morin, Keiser, Pryor, Chicopee, Oswald, Crockett, Bowler, Scribner) is not drawn. It carried Cody's passenger trains for ten years and appears in the 1902 timetable, but the alignment was lifted in April 1911 and is not mapped in OpenStreetMap, so it would have to be a mostly-guessed line; it is left out rather than drawn badly.

The 1911-onward approach from Billings via Fromberg, Bridger and Warren into Frannie IS now drawn - see cbq_big_horn_basin_line.geojson, feature cbq-frannie-billings - so this branch is no longer orphaned: its junction end sits 8.7 m off the cbq-frannie-kirby feature, which is simplification residue, not a gap. Still not drawn: the Colorado and Southern half of the Shoshone's route south of Orin Junction.
The exact site of the 1901 Cody depot was not located; the trace stops at today's end of track.

properties.line: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy: Cody Branch
properties.speed_source: estimated: a 42-mile branch local with five intermediate stops (Mantua, Garland, Powell, Ralston, Corbett); no timetable running time was checked. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_quality: REAL TRACE, no approximated legs. Stitched from the 38 OpenStreetMap ways tagged name='BNSF Cody Subdivision' (railway=rail, usage=branch) - the surviving ex-CB&Q Cody Branch, still in service for freight - into one continuous LineString with zero gaps (largest way-to-way join 0 m) and no reversal or revisit artifacts, then simplified to a 15 m Douglas-Peucker tolerance (443 -> 53 points, 0.03 mi of length lost). Traced length 41.73 mi against 42.4 mi of documented mileage (98.4%). The 0.7 mi shortfall is at the two ends and is accounted for: the trace starts at the junction with the Casper Subdivision, 0.5 mi (810 m) short of the Frannie depot site, and stops at today's end of track on the northeast edge of Cody, about 1 mi (1650 m) from the town centre - the last stub into the 1901 depot site is not traced. Intermediate stations land on the trace at very nearly their timetable mileposts once that 0.5 mi head offset is allowed for: Garland 14.02 traced vs 14.8 documented (63 m off the line), Powell 19.18 vs 19.8 (271 m), Ralston 24.96 vs 25.8 (208 m). ERA CAVEAT: this is the modern alignment. It is the same corridor the branch has always used - the Cody Branch was never relocated - but any minor 20th-century line changes within it would be drawn in their modern form. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 1 ruled segment totalling 11 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: The Burlington reached Cody on November 11 1901, at the end of a 131-mile push begun in the spring of 1900 from Toluca, Montana (west of Hardin) - built to open the Big Horn Basin irrigation projects and to make Cody the eastern rail gateway to Yellowstone. In these first years the trains that served this branch came down over the Pryor Mountains from Toluca via Coburn, Pryor, Bowler and Scribner to Frannie; only the Frannie - Cody portion drawn here survives. The CB&Q began advertising the route as 'The Cody Road into Yellowstone Park' from a 1905 brochure. Headway is an estimate - a daily local is the usual pattern for a CB&Q branch of this length - and is not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the November 11 1901 first train, the spring-1900 start of construction, the 131-mile Toluca-Cody length and the Toluca-Pryor-Bowler-Scribner-Frannie station order are from the Pryor Mountains homestead-era railroad page; the 1905 'Cody Road' brochure and the Yellowstone-gateway purpose are from the Environment & Society Portal's CB&Q exhibition. Headway and speed are unsourced estimates.

segments.note: The Toluca - Warren approach over the Pryor Mountains was pulled up in April 1911 - blamed on the grade in Pryor Gap, slow running, and the awkwardness of connecting at Coburn rather than Billings - and replaced by 30 miles of new track from Fromberg to Warren, completed April 9 1911, which put Cody's trains onto the Clarks Fork valley route from Billings via Fromberg, Bridger and Warren into Frannie. The branch itself was untouched; only what it connected to changed. The Burlington began offering direct service to Yellowstone's east entrance in 1912 and built the Burlington Cody Cafe (opened June 20 1917) and the Cody Inn (June 19 1922) at the Cody end for park-bound passengers, with Yellowstone Park Transportation Co. motor coaches taking them the 96 road miles on to Lake Hotel. Mantua, Garland, Powell, Ralston, Corbett and Cody all appear in the 1909, 1925 and 1932 CB&Q public timetables. Headway estimated/unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: the April 1911 abandonment of Toluca-Warren, its stated reasons and the April 9 1911 completion of the Fromberg-Warren connection are from the Pryor Mountains homestead-era railroad page; the 1912 start of direct east-entrance service and the 96-mile Cody Road are from the Environment & Society Portal and geyserbob.com, which also date the Cody Cafe (June 20 1917) and Cody Inn (June 19 1922); the station list and 1909/1925/1932 public-timetable appearances are from John Fowler's Wyoming passenger stations compilation (SL 170), line 11 Frannie-Cody. Headway and speed are unsourced estimates.

segments.note: Service ran down. The branch is in the CB&Q's 1932 public timetable but gone from the 1950 one, so whatever ran over it in the last quarter-century was most likely an unadvertised mixed train rather than a scheduled passenger local - this is inference from the timetable compilation, not a sourced statement about the consist. The Burlington ended passenger service to Cody in 1956; the Cody Inn's furnishings were auctioned the following year and the building partly demolished. SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded not resolved: geyserbob.com and streamlinermemories both give 1956 as the end of passenger service, while the timetable compilation shows the branch's stations dropping out of the public timetable somewhere between 1932 and 1950. Both can be true if the last years were mixed-train only, but no source consulted says so outright. Freight continued after 1956 and still does - the line is BNSF's Cody Subdivision - which is why the drawn years stop here.
sources: Segment-level: the 1956 end of passenger service and the 1957 auction and partial demolition of the Cody Inn are from geyserbob.com; the presence of the branch's stations in the 1932 but not the 1950 CB&Q public timetable is from John Fowler's Wyoming passenger stations compilation (SL 170), line 11 Frannie-Cody. The mixed-train inference for 1932-1956 is NOT SOURCED. Headway and speed are unsourced estimates.
